title: Review a diff with 5 seeded bugs
goal: Run an AI review over a branch whose tests all pass but which hides five bugs, one of them a security issue. Triage the findings against evidence, and write down what the review caught, what it missed and what was noise.
setup_cmd: cp -r exercises/ex-3-3-review-seeded-bugs/starter ~/fm-ex/ex-3-3-review-seeded-bugs && cd ~/fm-ex/ex-3-3-review-seeded-bugs && git init -q -b main && echo change.patch >> .git/info/exclude && git add -A && git commit -qm base && git init -q --bare ../ex-3-3-origin.git && git remote add origin ../ex-3-3-origin.git && git push -q origin main && git remote set-head origin main && git checkout -q -b feature/orders && git apply --index change.patch && git commit -qm 'Add order handling' && npm test

starter_prompts.claude: The seeded change is committed on branch feature/orders, with a local origin whose default branch is main. Run /code-review high main...feature/orders, then /security-review (it diffs against origin/HEAD, which the setup created). Or ask: "Review the changes on this branch against main. Report only bugs that would break behaviour, each with file:line and an input that triggers it. Money is integer cents. Every SQL query must be parameterised. Ignore formatting." Save your triage in REVIEW.md: for each finding, the verdict (real, false positive, unproven) and your evidence.
starter_prompts.codex: The seeded change is committed on branch feature/orders. Run /review, pick "Review against a base branch" and choose main; then run /review again with "Custom review instructions". From the shell, use a scope flag alone (codex review --base main) or a prompt alone with the scope in the text, never both: codex review "Review the changes on this branch against main. Report only bugs that would break behaviour, each with file:line and an input that triggers it. Money is integer cents. Every SQL query must be parameterised. Ignore formatting." Then a security pass: codex review "Security review of this branch's diff against main only: injection, authn/authz gaps, data exposure. Give file:line and how to exploit each finding." Save your triage in REVIEW.md: for each finding, the verdict (real, false positive, unproven) and your evidence.

solution_notes: The reference REVIEW.md ranks the SQL injection first and gives a concrete trigger for every finding, for example page 1 returning ids 3 and 4.

Each finding is tied to something the change itself says: the 1-based doc comment, the 'a failed email must not undo the order' comment, and the 'sum of all refunds' comment. Reading comments as the spec is how the off-by-one, missing await and refund cap are found.
The existing tests pass because they check lengths and use round numbers. The fixed solution adds one test per finding, and each of those tests fails against the buggy code.
It separates blocking findings from follow-ups: unbounded result size and a missing transaction are noted, not treated as defects in this change.
